rules.title: AlwaysInstallElevated is on
rules.subject: AlwaysInstallElevated
rules.why: With both values set, Windows Installer runs every .msi with SYSTEM rights, whoever starts it.
rules.fix: Set both values to 0 or delete them. In Group Policy, turn off Windows Components > Windows Installer > 'Always install with elevated privileges' under both Computer and User Configuration.

rules.title: User Account Control is turned off
rules.subject: EnableLUA
rules.why: With UAC off, administrators run everything with full rights, so any code that runs in an admin's session is already elevated.

rules.title: Administrators elevate without a prompt
rules.subject: ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin
rules.why: Code running in an administrator's session can elevate silently, with no prompt for the user to notice.
rules.fix: Set ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin to 2 (always prompt, on the secure desktop) or 5 (the default).

rules.title: UAC prompts don't use the secure desktop
rules.subject: PromptOnSecureDesktop
rules.why: Other programs in the session can see and interact with the elevation prompt, or imitate it.

rules.title: Remote UAC restrictions are off for local accounts
rules.subject: LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy
rules.why: Local administrator accounts get a full admin token over the network, so a reused local admin password or hash gives remote admin access to this machine.
rules.fix: Set LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy to 0 or delete it, and give each machine a unique local admin password (Windows LAPS).

rules.title: WDigest keeps logon passwords in memory
rules.subject: UseLogonCredential
rules.why: Windows keeps the passwords of logged-on users in LSASS memory in a recoverable form, so anyone who reaches admin on this machine can read the plaintext passwords of everyone logged on.

rules.title: LSA protection isn't turned on by policy
rules.subject: RunAsPPL
rules.why: Without LSA protection, any admin process can read LSASS memory and the credentials in it.
rules.fix: Set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL to 1 (or 2 for no UEFI lock) and reboot, or turn on Local Security Authority protection under Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation. Newer Windows 11 builds can enable it without this value, so check that page first.

rules.title: Point and Print lets non-admins install printer drivers
rules.subject: PointAndPrint
rules.why: Non-admins can install printer drivers without an elevation prompt, and printer drivers run as SYSTEM. This is the configuration that kept PrintNightmare exploitable after the patch.
rules.fix: Set RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators to 1 (or delete it: 1 is the default on patched systems), and set NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall and UpdatePromptSettings to 0.

rules.title: Windows Update uses a WSUS server over plain HTTP
rules.subject: WUServer
rules.why: Updates come from WSUS over unencrypted HTTP. Anyone who can intercept that traffic can serve a fake update, which installs as SYSTEM.
rules.fix: Configure WSUS for HTTPS and point WUServer and WUStatusServer at the https:// address.

rules.title: LM and NTLMv1 authentication are allowed
rules.subject: LmCompatibilityLevel
rules.why: This machine will answer with LM or NTLMv1 responses, which are easy to crack or relay.
rules.fix: Set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 (send NTLMv2 only, refuse LM and NTLM), or at least 3.
